Nothing in `ces-revisions` produces a working outcome yet. The package is a greeting `main()` with two smoke tests, and there is no spec. So this is a new-project roadmap. Before writing any roadmap text, here are the outcomes and tracks for you to rank.

**Source.** No spec and no outcomes in your own words yet. Every outcome below is a candidate from your brief `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`; please confirm or drop each. The brief's Parts A and B (the literature review and gap analysis) are already delivered by the three research files, so I've treated those files as background, not as outcomes. I have only read the first 3,000 characters and the headings of each research file. Cost notes marked *inventory unread* would firm up once I read the data-availability sections (ChatGPT §3.3, Claude §3, Gemini Part B).

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | Track | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A real-time panel of CES employment by release vintage (1st, 2nd and 3rd print, preliminary and final benchmark), for total nonfarm and each supersector, NSA and SA, back as far as public archives reach | A | Total nonfarm: a few MB (one monthly series × several hundred vintages). Supersector NSA coverage: *inventory unread*. The brief notes BLS does not archive QCEW vintages. |
| O2 | Revision-magnitude history for each of the four stages over time (mean absolute revision, dispersion, tails), checked against BLS's published MAR table (48k→33k at 1st→2nd, per ChatGPT exec summary) | A | Small compute; depends on O1 |
| O3 | Long-run split of the one- and two-month SA revisions into an NSA-sample component and a seasonal-factor component. ChatGPT reports no published long-run decomposition exists. | B | Only running it can tell; depends on paired NSA/SA vintages existing (*inventory unread*) |
| O4 | Estimated effect of collection-interval days and first-closing rate on one-month revision dispersion | C | Collection days: computable from release and reference calendars. First-closing rates by month back in time: *inventory unread*. |
| O5 | Benchmark and wedge-back error by supersector over time, including the birth-death share | D | Benchmark articles are one per year, about 40 documents. Some figures will likely need hand extraction; that is your time, size unknown until one year is tried. |
| O6 | A hand-built panel of BLS operational capacity (real appropriations, FTE, sample size, shutdown/CR months) and its descriptive association with revision scale, explicitly non-causal | E | Your time: about 40 fiscal years of budget justifications plus FedScope. Most likely the largest manual cost in the project. |
| O7 | The joint multi-vintage Bayesian state-space model: latent truth, stage-specific news/noise, Student-t measurement with covariate-driven stochastic log-scale, supersector partial pooling, benchmark as an irregular observation | F | NUTS cost (11 supersectors × ~500 months × 4 stages × NSA/SA): only running it can tell |
| O8 | Evidence on whether the covariates in scale earn their place: LOO/PSIS against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks, revision-dispersion posterior predictive checks | F | Repeated fits of O7; scales with O7's measured cost |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, full validation suites, scheduled monthly refresh.

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Vintage data and revision history** (known progression). Everything else reads from it.
- **B — Seasonal factor vs. sample** (research).
- **C — Collection interval** (research).
- **D — Benchmark and wedge-back** (research).
- **E — Operational capacity, descriptive** (research).
- **F — Joint state-space model** (research).

**Why the split:** B, C, D and E each answer a question that stands without the others, even though all of them explain revision scale. Folded into F, as the brief bundles them, each of those answers would wait on the full joint model's machinery. F stays its own track because it adds something none of them give: news and noise identified jointly across stages with uncertainty about the truth. It is also the outcome whose cost is most open.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 via uv; pytest and ruff (repo).
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax, ArviZ, Polars (brief, Part C).
- Units in thousands of jobs (brief).
- Capacity covariates and the party of the appropriators are descriptive groupings, not causal slopes (brief).

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file with that name exists yet.

**Optional probe, only if you say yes:** I could read the three data-inventory sections and pull one real ALFRED vintage list for PAYEMS. That would turn the *inventory unread* notes into actual figures.

**What I need from you:** rank the outcomes within each track and rank the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the outcomes, the tracks, their kinds, and the name.
